Participants anticipated monetary and drug-related incentives and pressed a key while a target was on screen; premature responses occurred during the anticipation phase.

During the monetary incentive block, participants responded during the 3,000–5,000 ms anticipation period before the target appeared, rather than waiting to press the key while the brief white-square target was on screen; this was an impulsive response and did not satisfy the target-response demand.

During the monetary incentive block, participants waited through the anticipation period and pressed a key while the brief white-square target was on screen; trials were matched to premature monetary trials by trial type and proximity.

During the drug-incentive block, participants responded during the 3,000–5,000 ms anticipation period before the target appeared, rather than waiting to press the key while the brief white-square target was on screen; this was an impulsive response and did not satisfy the target-response demand.

During the drug-incentive block, participants waited through the anticipation period and pressed a key while the brief white-square target was on screen; trials were matched to premature drug-incentive trials by trial type and proximity.

instructions.value: Participants were required to press a key while the target was still on screen.
